1. (Currently amended) A method for controlling a flow of air, the method comprising: establishing a level of vacuum in a booster device by generating the flow of air from the booster device using a pump; determining whether the level of vacuum in the booster device has reached a predetermined value; terminating the flow of air from the booster device when the level of vacuum in the booster device has reached the predetermined value; and __maintaining the level of vacuum in the booster device by preventing re-establishment of air flow into the booster device after termination__.

2. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, wherein said terminating the flow of air is accomplished via a directional control valve __that is responsive to a pressure sensor detecting the predetermined vacuum level__, such that a pressure differential across the pump is reduced.

3. (Currently amended) The method of claim 2, wherein said terminating the flow of air includes __simultaneously__ changing the direction of the flow of air and closing a flow path between the pump and the booster device__by a single actuation of the directional control valve__.

4. (Currently amended) The method of claim 3, wherein said changing the direction of the flow of air includes opening a flow path between a negative pressure chamber of the pump and a positive pressure chamber of the pump __in a manner that prevents vacuum from being re-established in the booster device__.

5. (Currently amended) The method of claim 3, wherein said changing the direction of the flow of air includes opening a path for a flow of air between the pump and the atmosphere __through a controlled vent that prevents backflow into the booster device__.

6. (Currently amended) The method of claim 5, further comprising filtering the flow of air between the atmosphere and the pump via a filter __positioned to prevent particulate contamination of the pump during the venting operation__.

7. (Original) The method of claim 1, wherein the booster device is a vacuum servo booster for an automobile braking system.

8. (Currently amended) A system for controlling a flow of air, the system comprising: a booster device configured to provide a vacuum assist when a level of vacuum has been established in the device; a pump configured to establish the level of vacuum in the booster device by generating the flow of air from the booster device; __a pressure sensor configured to detect when the level of vacuum in the booster device has reached a predetermined value__; and a directional control valve adapted to terminate the flow of air from the booster device __in response to the pressure sensor__ when the level of vacuum in the booster device has reached a predetermined value, such that a pressure differential across the pump is reduced __and the vacuum level is maintained__.

9. (Currently amended) The system of claim 8, wherein the directional control valve is further adapted to __simultaneously__ change the direction of the flow of air and close a flow path between the pump and the booster device __upon a single actuation event triggered by the pressure sensor__.

10. (Currently amended) The system of claim 9, wherein to change the direction of the flow of air the directional control valve opens a flow path between a negative pressure chamber of the pump and a positive pressure chamber of the pump __in a manner that prevents re-evacuation of the booster device__.

11. (Currently amended) The system of claim 9, wherein to change the direction of the flow of air the directional control valve opens a flow path between the pump and the atmosphere __through a controlled vent mechanism__.

12. (Currently amended) The system of claim 11, further comprising a filter adapted for filtering a flow of air between the atmosphere and the pump __to prevent contamination during venting__.

13. (Original) The system of claim 8, wherein the booster device is a vacuum servo booster for an automobile braking system.

14. (Currently amended) A motor vehicle comprising: an internal combustion engine; a booster device configured to provide a vacuum assist when a level of vacuum has been established in the device; __a pressure sensor configured to detect when the level of vacuum in the booster device has reached a predetermined value__; and a system for controlling a flow of air from the booster device, the system including: a pump configured to establish the level of vacuum in the booster device by generating the flow of air from the booster device; and a directional control valve adapted to terminate the flow of air from the booster device __in response to the pressure sensor__ when the level of vacuum in the booster device has reached a predetermined value, such that a pressure differential across the pump and a parasitic load on the engine are reduced __and the vacuum level is maintained without re-evacuation__.

15. (Currently amended) The vehicle of claim 14, wherein the directional control valve is further adapted to __simultaneously__ change the direction of the flow of air and close a flow path between the pump and the booster device __upon a single actuation event triggered by the pressure sensor__.

16. (Currently amended) The vehicle of claim 15, wherein to change the direction of the flow of air the directional control valve opens a flow path between a negative pressure chamber of the pump and a positive pressure chamber of the pump __in a manner that prevents re-evacuation of the booster device__.

17. (Currently amended) The vehicle of claim 15, wherein to change the direction of the flow of air the directional control valve opens a flow path between the pump and the atmosphere __through a controlled vent mechanism__.

18. (Currently amended) The vehicle of claim 17, further comprising a filter adapted for filtering the flow of air between the atmosphere and the pump __to prevent contamination during venting__.

19. (Original) The vehicle of claim 14, further comprising a braking system, wherein the booster device is a vacuum servo booster for the braking system.
